case_analysis.thread_summary: ATAGO Co. quoting thread (214 lines). Three distinct customer questions: (1) whether their GATT-based profile requires PTS testing (answered: depends on UUID type — 16-bit → test required; 128-bit → no test); (2) optimal registration timing for a September launch (answered: register ~3 months early, can set Submission Date up to 90 days in the future); (3) whether they can change the SIG account email (answered: not possible — must register new account; both accounts can coexist). Thread also confirmed ATAGO is a SIG Adopter member and has an existing valid End Product registration (D041005, BT v5.0).
all_questions_found: Does a GATT Base Profile require SIG PTS testing?
How far in advance can we register and when is the right time relative to product launch?
Can we change the email address on an existing SIG member account?
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: UUID type determines profile test requirement: SIG-assigned 16-bit UUID → PTS test required; proprietary 128-bit UUID → no test. This is the definitive scoping rule for profile test inclusion.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: Three independent rules: (1) 16-bit vs 128-bit UUID determines test scope; (2) 90-day advance registration window protects against new SIG rules; (3) SIG email is immutable — new account is the only option.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Misclassifying a 16-bit UUID profile as proprietary would result in an under-tested product. Waiting too long before launch risks being caught by new Consistency Check rules. Failing to create a new account for email changes leaves customers unable to use their preferred email.
case_analysis.consulting_mistake: No mistakes identified. Sakai provided clear, correct answers to all three questions.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Always ask customers for the UUID value (or type) of any profile they list on an RFQ — this single data point determines whether PTS testing is required. For registration timing, proactively recommend the 3-month-before-launch rule even if the customer does not ask.
